items.q: What is Conway's law, tightly stated?
items.a: Designs copy **information-transfer paths**. Inside one head is fastest; **more hops, more seams**.

items.q: Why would Conway still apply to AI agents?
items.a: Agents have **slower links** through tools, tests and compilers, so the system will show **seams at those links**.

items.q: What does Hyrum's law say about APIs?
items.a: With enough users, **every observable behaviour** will be depended on, **not just the written contract**.

sections.title: Laws that do not survive a closer look

items.q: How did the panel treat Brooks' law?
items.a: As **unreliable**: adding people can delay a late project in a bureaucracy, but it is **not always true**.
People will **not use an information system** when opening it is more painful than **staying ignorant**.

items.q: What happened to Eagleson's 'stranger to your own code in six months'?
items.a: Prime now rates it **F**: with AI he often **never looks at the code** at all.

items.q: How should you treat named programming laws?
items.a: As **heuristics**, not physics. Many are **context-dependent** or **unreliable**.

items.q: What is Annie's wrinkle on Cunningham's law?
items.a: **Ask the question nicely first**, then add a **confidently wrong** reply if you need a fast correction.

items.q: When does Goodhart bite in software?
items.a: When a **fuzzy metric** (watch time, tokens used) becomes the **target** and stops measuring what you cared about.
